concepts.name: fractions
concepts.description: Fractions represent parts of a whole. Numerator (top) = parts you have. Denominator (bottom) = total equal parts.
concepts.examples: 1/2 of a pizza means 1 slice out of 2 equal slices. 3/4 means 3 out of 4 parts.
concepts.common_mistakes: Confusing numerator and denominator. Thinking bigger denominator means bigger fraction.

concepts.name: common denominators
concepts.description: A common denominator is a shared multiple of two denominators. Needed to add or subtract fractions.
concepts.examples: For 1/2 and 1/3, common denominators are 6, 12, 18. LCD is 6. 1/2 = 3/6, 1/3 = 2/6.
concepts.common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply both numerator AND denominator. Adding denominators instead of finding common ones.

concepts.name: fraction addition
concepts.description: To add fractions: 1) Make denominators the same. 2) Add numerators. 3) Keep denominator. 4) Simplify if needed.
concepts.common_mistakes: Adding numerators and denominators separately (1/2 + 1/3 ≠ 2/5). Forgetting to find common denominator.

concepts.name: equivalent fractions
concepts.description: Equivalent fractions have the same value but different numerators and denominators. Found by multiplying/dividing both by same number.
concepts.common_mistakes: Only multiplying numerator. Thinking 1/2 and 2/5 are equivalent because 1+1=2 and 2+3=5.

concepts.name: simplifying fractions
concepts.description: Simplifying means reducing to lowest terms by dividing numerator and denominator by their GCD.
concepts.common_mistakes: Not dividing by the greatest common divisor. Stopping too early.
